title: Electrical Inspection Checklist and OSHA Requirements (29 CFR 1910.303)
subtitle: For routine walk-throughs of panels, switchboards, disconnects and electrical rooms, with key checks for installations over 600 V.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A, and note the location and equipment for each defect.
When an item fails, keep people clear of any exposed live parts, record the defect and assign the correction before the equipment returns to normal use.
The manufacturer's instructions, other Subpart S sections and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Equipment condition and markings
items: Installation and use match the instructions supplied with the listed or labeled product
Manufacturer name or trademark and voltage, current or wattage ratings are present and readable
Every unused opening in boxes, cabinets, raceways and housings is closed with protection equal to the enclosure wall
No broken, bent, cut, corroded or overheated parts affecting safe operation or strength
No paint, plaster, cleaner, abrasive or corrosive residue on busbars, terminals or insulators
Equipment is firmly secured to its surface and not held by wooden plugs in masonry, concrete or plaster
Ventilating openings are not blocked by walls, stored items or adjacent equipment
Equipment in damp, wet, corrosive or high-temperature locations is identified for that environment

sections.title: Connections and splices
items: Pressure connectors, splicing connectors and soldering lugs are identified for the conductor material and correctly installed
Copper and aluminum conductors do not touch in one connector unless the device is identified for that use
Conductors are terminated without damage using pressure connectors, solder lugs or splices to flexible leads; binding screws only on No. 10 or smaller
Terminals holding more than one conductor, and terminals on aluminum, are identified for that use
Splices, joints and free conductor ends are covered with equivalent insulation or an identified insulating device; no bare joints

sections.title: Disconnects and circuit marking
items: Each service, feeder and branch circuit is legibly labeled with its purpose at its breaker, fuse or disconnect, unless the purpose is evident
Each required disconnect for motors and appliances shows what it controls, unless its purpose is evident
Disconnect and circuit labels are intact and readable in the room's conditions
Each required disconnect can accept a lock in the open (off) position
Enclosures with series combination rated breakers or fuses carry the readily visible field caution marking

sections.title: Working space and clearance (600 V or less)
items: No boxes, carts, pallets or materials kept in the working space in front of panels, switchboards and other equipment
Depth in front of live parts or the enclosure front meets Table S-1: at least 3.0 ft up to 150 V to ground; 3.0, 3.5 or 4.0 ft at 151-600 V by condition
Space is as wide as the equipment or 30 in., whichever is greater, and doors swing to 90 degrees or more
Nothing intrudes from floor to headroom height except associated electrical equipment projecting 6 in. or less
At least 6.5 ft (6.25 ft for installations before August 13, 2007), or the equipment height if taller
Working space at indoor panels, switchboards and motor control centers is lit; equipment-room lights are not on automatic control only
The working space has at least one entrance of sufficient area
No foreign pipes, ducts or equipment in the panel footprint up to 6.0 ft above it or the structural ceiling, unless isolated or protected

sections.title: Guarding of live parts
items: Live parts at 50 volts or above are in approved enclosures with covers in place, or guarded by a qualified-only room, partitions, an elevated platform, or 8.0 ft or more of elevation
Equipment exposed to physical damage has guards or enclosures strong enough to prevent it
Doors to rooms with exposed live parts carry conspicuous signs forbidding entry by unqualified persons
Parts that arc or spark in normal operation are enclosed or separated from combustible material
Over-600 V rooms and enclosures with exposed live parts are locked or under constant observation by a qualified person
Permanent, conspicuous high-voltage danger signs at those entrances
